title: (Senior) Data & Analytics Engineer - m/f/d
description:
Where Europe's enterprises adopt AI

Langdock is the AI platform used by more than 10,000 companies to give employees secure access to the leading AI models, to build and share agents and to automate repetitive workflows. We have grown past $40M ARR while remaining a small team, and we care deeply about operating efficiently across the entire company.

For many enterprises, Langdock is becoming the place where most of the net-new work is produced. As people and agents create more documents, analyses, decisions, and automations inside AI interfaces, the context and data behind that work accumulate within Langdock. This gives us the opportunity to earn a larger role in their technology stack by building a platform they choose to rely on.

Our ambition is to build that platform for European enterprises while preserving their control over data, model providers, and deployment environments. We have made meaningful progress at the application layer, but much of the foundation beneath it still needs to be built.

You can watch the Meet the engineering team video to get a feeling for how we work.

The role

Data at Langdock sits close to Product Development because our product is our core business. Understanding how people use Langdock requires detailed product context, especially as the product evolves quickly and raw events can be easy to misinterpret.

As our first dedicated data hire, you will own the path from raw data to trusted decisions. You will sit between product and engineering, combining data engineering, analytics engineering, product analytics, and technical platform ownership.

You will not start from scratch. We already run the dbt transformation framework on ClickHouse, ingest product, billing, and customer data, and provide business-facing marts and Metabase dashboards. Your role is to turn these foundations into a reliable data system that the company can trust and build on.

What you will own

-
Make company metrics trustworthy. Define and model metrics so people understand what each number means, how it is calculated, and where its limitations are. Resolve inconsistencies and prevent teams from working with conflicting definitions.

-
Build a reliable model of product usage. Develop a deep understanding of Langdock's products and translate raw application data into useful models for activation, adoption, retention, feature usage, and customer health.

-
Own the data platform in production. Build and operate ingestion pipelines, warehouse models, data quality checks, deployment workflows, and monitoring. Ensure that data remains accurate, fresh, observable, and available when people depend on it.

-
Partner with Product Engineers. Help product squads understand how people use what they build, answer exploratory questions, evaluate product changes, and identify opportunities or problems that are not obvious from individual customer conversations.

-
Improve product instrumentation. Find blind spots in the data we collect and work with engineers to design events and source data that make future analysis reliable.

-
Serve the company's core data consumers. Enable Account Management to understand adoption within specific accounts, help Revenue and Finance understand where the company makes money, and provide leadership with dependable company-level reporting.

-
Create self-service foundations. Build clear marts, documentation, and dashboards that let teams answer recurring questions without requiring a custom analysis each time.

What makes this role different

This is neither a dashboard-only analytics role nor an infrastructure-only data engineering role. You will own the complete system, from how product data is generated to how a metric is interpreted in a product or business decision.

The hardest part is not writing SQL or operating ClickHouse. It is developing enough product and business context to model ambiguous data correctly while building technical systems that remain dependable as Langdock changes quickly.

Because this is our first dedicated data hire, you will establish the standards for data modeling, quality, ownership, observability, and collaboration across Product Development.

What success could look like

Within your first year:

-
Product, Account Management, RevOps, and leadership use consistent definitions for the company's most important metrics.

-
Product squads can understand adoption and behavior without questioning whether the underlying data is correct.

-
Important pipelines and models have explicit owners, tests, freshness expectations, monitoring, and recovery procedures.

-
Gaps in product instrumentation are identified and addressed as part of product development.

-
Recurring questions are answered through reusable models and dashboards rather than one-off queries.

-
The company has a clear technical direction for how the data platform should evolve.

What we are looking for

-
You have built and operated production data pipelines and analytical models, not only consumed data prepared by others.

-
You can move between infrastructure, SQL modeling, exploratory analysis, and conversations about product or business definitions.

-
You treat data quality and metric definitions as product responsibilities.

-
You are comfortable working with dbt, analytical databases, deployment systems, and business intelligence tools.

-
You investigate surprising numbers until you understand the underlying product behavior and technical mechanism.

-
You can turn an ambiguous question into a clear definition, a dependable model, and an actionable explanation.

-
You want broad ownership and are motivated by establishing the foundations for a growing data function.

Working here

This is an in-office role at Greifswalder Strasse 212 in Berlin. We work together in person because it helps us build trust, develop shared context, and make decisions quickly.

Most engineers start around 8:30. We usually eat lunch together, and dinner is available for people who stay later. Running and gym are part of the routine for many of us.

You need an existing right to work in Germany. We do not currently sponsor visas.

Compensation

The salary range for this role is €90,000–€140,000 gross per year, depending on level and scope. All roles include equity. Salaries are tied to levels, not negotiation.

We will figure out the right level together based on your experience and scope. Levels are about the work you own, not your title or years of experience.

description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Please submit your application by 5:00 pm EST on October 23rd, 2026

Intro to Position

You will be critical to building a new, leaner, audience-centric, data-driven app that serves NPR and partnering stations in multi-modal formats. As the Senior Insights Analyst, Mobile Analytics, you will drive data-informed decision-making for the NPR App, serving as the core owner of platform experimentation and advanced mobile product analytics.

Central to this role is high-level SQL mastery. You will extract actionable insights from complex, unaggregated datasets—frequently writing advanced queries (e.g., raw GA4 and Firebase exports in BigQuery) for deep cohort, behavioral, and retention analyses. Additionally, you will establish quality control standards for SQL execution across the team, train colleagues on query optimization, and design end-to-end A/B tests that expand weekly audiences, deepen listening habits, and maximize revenue yield.

This role reports to the Audience Insights Senior Manager, Product.

This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with NABET-CWA DMU.

Responsibilities

- Advanced SQL & Raw Data Engineering: Write, optimize, and QC complex SQL queries using BigQuery; transform raw event logs, access nested arrays, and perform advanced cohort, pattern, and behavioral analysis across app and web platforms.

- Experimentation Ownership: Lead the experimentation lifecycle on NPR’s owned and operated platforms using Optimizely (or comparable tools); partner across teams to formulate hypotheses, design rigorous A/B testing frameworks, run experiments, and translate results into product recommendations.

- Product Insights & Strategy: Deliver foundational trend reporting and deep-dive mobile app analytics to product managers, newsroom leaders, and station stakeholders to advocate for audience needs and guide strategy.

- Technical Mentorship & Enablement: Share advanced SQL and analytical expertise with teammates; build sustainable self-service insight tools and train cross-functional partners to utilize data effectively in daily decision-making.

- Data Infrastructure & QC: Streamline scheduled queries, data summaries, and automated pipelines; partner with Data Products to diagnose and resolve tracking anomalies and optimize tool design based on user needs.

- Workload & Stakeholder Prioritization: Manage incoming analytical requests by evaluating business impact, aligning deliverables directly with departmental strategy and media landscape trends.

- Culture & Best Practices: Proactively share research tools and insights to cultivate a transparent, data-driven learning culture across NPR and partner stations nationwide.

- Documentation & Standards: Establish guidelines, data dictionaries, and technical documentation for app, video, and web metrics to ensure organizational reporting consistency.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

- 5+ years of advanced SQL experience: Demonstrated expertise writing complex SQL queries from scratch, querying raw, unaggregated event logs, and utilizing data warehousing environments (e.g., BigQuery, Dataform).

- Raw Data & Array Manipulation Expertise: Proven ability to fetch, transform, and manipulate complex data structures, taking raw data to create audience cohorts and behavioral pattern modeling.

- 5+ years of Mobile & Web Analytics: Hands-on experience with app and digital behavioral analytics datasets (e.g., Google Firebase, GA4) across mobile product environments.

- 2+ years of Experimentation Design: Demonstrated experience formulating, executing, and evaluating A/B and multivariate tests using enterprise platforms (e.g., Optimizely).

- Data Visualization & Reporting: Expert proficiency in converting complex SQL outputs into clear visual stories (Looker, Tableau) and advanced spreadsheet models (Excel/Google Sheets) for non-technical stakeholders.

- Stakeholder Enablement & Training: Proven track record of training partners on data tools, establishing self-service frameworks, and mentoring peers on SQL and data hygiene best practices.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience within digital news media, public broadcasting, or media streaming platforms.

- Statistical modeling proficiency using scripting languages such as R or Python.

- Demonstrated success in building cross-functional partnerships to solve complex, multi-departmental analytical problems.

Required Skills/Competencies

- Advanced SQL & Raw Data Extraction: Exceptional ability to write efficient SQL to unnest arrays, parse JSON/struct fields, and build scalable datasets from raw event-level digital behavior.

- Experimental Methodology: Deep competency in A/B testing design, statistical significance testing, hypothesis formulation, and post-test behavioral analysis.

You will lead the implementation of stateful multi-agent workflows, leveraging frontier LLMs (with a strong emphasis on the Anthropic Claude ecosystem), Model Context Protocol (MCP), and modern orchestration engines to bridge complex business requirements with robust software engineering.

This role is critical to transforming enterprise business processes by embedding safe, high-accuracy, and deterministic autonomous AI agents into Salesforce CRM, Data Cloud, and core operational systems. Key Responsibilities

Architect stateful multi-agent coordination graphs using LangGraph or custom DAG loops, supporting dynamic task decomposition, supervisor orchestration, human-in-the-loop escalation, and automated error recovery.

-

Build standardized MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and connectors to securely expose Salesforce tools, objects, custom actions, and operational context to agent runners.

-

Optimize query routes and context engineering across model tiers (such as Claude Sonnet/Opus for multi-turn reasoning vs. Haiku for high-throughput utility tasks) to optimize latency, accuracy, and token spend.

-

Implement full-stack observability and defense-in-depth security using tools like LangSmith or Langfuse alongside strict input sanitization, field-level security (FLS), and automated PII scrubbing.

-

Lead technical delivery standards, establishing API interface contracts, specification-driven development patterns, and architectural blueprints for cross-functional engineering teams and executive stakeholders.

Requirements

7+ years of hands-on enterprise software engineering experience using Python, TypeScript/Node.js, Java, or Apex.

3+ years of direct production experience building, evaluating, and scaling LLM-powered applications and autonomous multi-agent workflows.

Tech Stack: Expert proficiency with LangGraph / LangChain, Anthropic/Claude APIs (tool calling, prompt caching, Claude Code), MCP, and observability tools (LangSmith, Langfuse, or OpenTelemetry).

Evaluation Frameworks: Hands-on experience with automated LLM eval suites (Promptfoo, Ragas, or LLM-as-a-judge patterns) as automated test gates.

Ownership mindset with deep diagnostic debugging skills for isolating non-deterministic LLM behavior, context degradation, and latency bottlenecks.

Experience deploying containerized MCP servers integrated with enterprise CRM security boundaries.

title: Data Engineering Manager
description:
About LILT

AI is changing how the world communicates — and LILT is leading that transformation.

We're on a mission to make the world's information accessible to everyone, regardless of the language they speak. We use cutting-edge AI, machine translation, and human-in-the-loop expertise to translate content faster, more accurately, and more cost-effectively without compromising on brand, voice, or quality.

At LILT, we empower our teammates with leading tools, global collaboration, and growth opportunities to do their best work. Our company virtues—Work together, win together; Find a way or make one; Dance in the customer's shoes; Quicker than they expect; Quality is Job 1—guide everything we do. We are trusted by Intel Corporation, Canva, the United States Department of Defense, the United States Air Force, ASICS, and hundreds of global Enterprises. Backed by Sequoia, Intel Capital, and Redpoint, we’re building a category-defining company in a $50B+ global translation market being redefined by AI.

About the Role

You own LILT's data transformation layer: the dbt layer and warehouse behind every number LILT reports, from Analytics to our LLM/MCP surface to internal dashboards. Metric definitions are often owned by other teams; you implement and keep them consistent. This layer has no owner today; you make it a role.

You lead a new Data sub-team in Platform Engineering, reporting to the head of Platform, as a hands-on player-manager while hiring and growing a Data Engineer and Senior Data Scientist. You hold decision rights over the transformation layer and warehouse and own their cost.

What You're Walking Into

We want to be direct about this role so the right person applies.

-
You inherit ambiguity. No single owner, pipelines to document and rebuild, and no team until your first two hires; until then you write the SQL, dbt, and Python yourself.

-
You settle the numbers. Finance, Operations, Production, and Product must trust the same metrics; you keep definitions consistent and say no when needed.

-
Some things are fixed, most aren't. dbt, a single warehouse, and on-prem parity are non-negotiable; warehouse cost is measured and expected to go down. Everything else is yours to decide, with a written case.

The Stack

-
Transformation: dbt on BigQuery

-
Analytics serving: ClickHouse, Cloud for SaaS, self-hosted on-prem

-
Sources: MySQL, replicated to BigQuery

-
ETL/orchestration: Python 3, Argo Workflows on Kubernetes

-
Consumers: In-app Analytics, Sigma, LILT's Assist agent, LILT's MCP server

-
Observability: Datadog

-
Agentic engineering: Claude Code and Cursor, used daily across Engineering

Key Responsibilities

-
Own the data layer. Implement every metric definition once in dbt, consistent everywhere it's used, partnering with the teams that define them. Business Operations, Production, Finance, and Product get one point of accountability; discrepancies resolve at the definition.

-
Run the transformation layer and warehouse: every pipeline has an owner, tests, and a known cost; spend is measured and goes down.

-
Set direction: warehouse strategy, ClickHouse's role, and how the layer is exposed via API and MCP, each backed by a written case.

-
Build the team: hire a Data Engineer and a Senior Data Scientist, set the charter, and run delivery, quality, and on-call health.

-
Set agentic engineering practice: define how the Data team uses AI agents to build, test, and review pipelines and models, including where human review is required.

-
Stay hands-on: read, review, and write the SQL, dbt, and Python your team ships.

Qualifications

-
People management: 7+ years in data/analytics engineering, including 2+ years managing a small team (2-5), with a track record of hiring and developing ICs.

-
Hands-on fundamentals: fluent in SQL and Python; has built and run production pipelines and a dbt (or equivalent) transformation layer; comfortable with BigQuery, ClickHouse, Snowflake, or similar.

-
Cost and roadmap ownership: has owned a warehouse or pipeline budget and reduced it with measurable results; translates business needs into a technical plan and sequences a backlog against limited headcount.

-
Stakeholder and business metrics: has owned data accountability for finance, operations, and go-to-market stakeholders, and understands B2B SaaS metrics (ARR, ACV, gross margin, on-time delivery) and how definition drift breaks them.

-
Effective AI use and communication: uses AI tools daily and knows where they help, mislead, and need verification; documents decisions clearly and communicates tradeoffs, risk, and cost crisply to leadership.

Preferred Skills

-
Stood up a data function from zero, or revived an abandoned one.

-
Run dbt in production at scale on BigQuery; operated ClickHouse.

-
Shipped analytics that runs in both cloud and self-hosted environments.

Our Story

Our founders, Spence and John met at Google working on Google Translate. As researchers at Stanford and Berkeley, they both worked on language technology to make information accessible to everyone. While together at Google, they were amazed to learn that Google Translate wasn’t used for enterprise products and services inside the company.The quality just wasn’t there. So they set out to build something better. LILT was born.

LILT has been a machine learning company since its founding in 2015. At the time, machine translation didn’t meet the quality standard for enterprise translations, so LILT assembled a cutting-edge research team tasked with closing that gap. While meeting customer demand for translation services, LILT has prioritized investments in Large Language Models, human-in-the-loop systems, and now agentic AI.

With AI innovation accelerating and enterprise demand growing, the next phase of LILT’s journey is just beginning.

Our Tech

What sets our platform apart:

-
Brand-aware AI that learns your voice, tone, and terminology to ensure every translation is accurate and consistent

-
Agentic AI workflows that automate the entire translation process from content ingestion to quality review to publishing

-
100+ native integrations with systems like Adobe Experience Manager, Webflow, Salesforce, GitHub, and Google Drive to simplify content translation

-
Human-in-the-loop reviews via our global network of professional linguists, for high-impact content that requires expert review

LILT in the News

-
Featured in The Software Report’s Top 100 Software Companies!

-
LILT makes it onto the Inc. 5000 List.

-
LILT’s continues to be an intellectual powerhouse, holding numerous patents that help power the most efficient and sophisticated AI and language models in the industry.

-
Check out all our news on our website.

title: Director, Global Hospital and Biosimilars (GH&B) Digital - End to End Data Architect
description:
ROLE SUMMARY

You will play a critical role in shaping the data foundation for Pfizer’s GH&B business by designing an integrated, scalable architecture that connects manufacturing, finance, supply, pricing and commercial performance data across the end-to-end value chain. You will define target-state data architecture, establish cross-domain data models, standards, data contracts and governance practices, and guide engineering teams in building trusted, reusable data products that support business decision-making today while remaining aligned to Pfizer’s evolving enterprise data strategy.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

-
Define and maintain the target state data architecture and multi-year roadmap for GH&B across the raw, mastered and cross domain layers, spanning manufacturing, finance and commercial, working with business partners, domain data owners, and the owners of PGS, commercial and enabling function data standards.

-
Set and apply data standards for GH&B in coordination with enterprise, manufacturing, commercial, and enabling function data standards owners, and represent GH&B Digital in architecture and data governance forums. Recommend GH&B originated patterns for reuse across Pfizer.

-
Define and maintain the GH&B cross domain data model that connects manufacturing, finance and commercial. This is the layer unique to GH&B and it is the core of the role.

-
Define data products, data contracts, schema standards and data movement rules across organizational and jurisdictional boundaries, including data residency and reporting constraints, and establish the criteria by which a GH&B data product is accepted as trusted.

-
Set DataOps and quality standards, and direct contractor data engineering capacity building and running the GH&B cross domain layer to those standards.

-
Apply and maintain data governance for a GxP (Good Practice quality regulations) environment, including data integrity by design and readiness for emerging regulatory expectations on AI and data.

-
Design for migration into enterprise platforms. Build interim, migration ready data contracts rather than permanent bespoke infrastructure, and hold a recurring checkpoint with the enterprise data fabric and institutional memory platform teams so GH&B structures stay compatible.

-
Lead architecture review for GH&B data initiatives, guide build versus conforms decisions, and prevent duplicative builds against enterprise platforms and against domain owned layers.

-
Direct contingent contractor data engineering resources, flexing with demand.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

-
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Management or a related field and 8+ years experience in data architecture, data management or data engineering, including experience setting standards adopted by teams outside their direct control

-
Relevant Masters degree and 7+ years experience in data architecture, data management or data engineering, including experience setting standards adopted by teams outside their direct control

-
Demonstrated leadership of enterprise data architecture, data models and data standards in a large, federated organization.

-
Experience defining architecture that spans more than one business domain, with distributed data ownership.

-
Experience applying data governance in a GxP or comparable regulated environment, including data integrity requirements.

-
Applied knowledge of AI concepts and a working understanding of what AI ready demands of data architecture.

-
Experience directing external engineering resources, partners or contractors.

-
Track record of influencing and aligning senior stakeholders across business and technology organizations without direct authority.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

-
Advanced degree (MS / MBA / PhD) in a relevant field.

-
Exposure to both commercial and manufacturing or supply chain data environments. Both is strongly preferred, and rare.

-
Working knowledge of data product and data contract practices, and of medallion layer architectures.

-
Experience with Snowflake, cloud data platforms and modern DataOps practice.

-
Working knowledge of ISA-95 / ISA-88 (the international standards for enterprise control system integration and batch control).

-
Recognized architecture or data management credentials (for example TOGAF, DAMA CDMP).

-
Participation in enterprise architecture governance or architecture review boards.

WORK LOCATION ASSIGNMENT: Must be able to work in assigned Pfizer office an average of 2.5 days per week, or as needed by the business.

PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS

N/A

-
Must be able to travel to Pfizer offices, vendor offices and other team meeting locations when required.

-
Project work can sometimes be demanding and require work during off-hours.

-
Regular meetings with EU and US based stakeholders.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
description:
About Checkr
Checkr is building the data platform to power safe and fair decisions. Over 140,000 companies and millions of people rely on Checkr for AI verification in the moments that matter most: getting a new job, a new place to live, a car ride, childcare, even a date. Customers include Uber, Pennymac, Airbnb, Doordash, and Anthropic.

We’re a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company.

About the team/role

We’re hiring an ML Engineer (P3) to build and ship the AI systems that power Checkr’s core products. This role sits on the ML team inside Checkr’s Data & ML organization within Engineering.

Checkr runs millions of background checks a year. The ML team builds the systems that make those checks faster, more accurate, and cheaper to operate: document processing, charge classification, entity resolution, and in-product intelligence. These are production services that Product Engineering depends on daily.

This is not a research role or a notebook role. You’ll own ML services end-to-end: design them, code them, deploy them, monitor them. We need someone who writes production software, builds with LLMs and APIs as first-class tools, and can tell the difference between working code and AI slop. If you’ve spent the last few years building AI-native software and you care deeply about engineering craft, we want to talk.

This role sits in the central Data & ML team within the Engineering organization. You will partner daily with Product Engineering, Product, and cross-functional teams. You’ll also contribute to Checkr’s broader AI strategy, including our initiative to deploy our agentic fleet and build scalable context with our semantic layer.

We are looking for someone based in San Francisco who has built ML systems in fast-moving, impact-first environments. Less process, more shipping. Less paperwork, more results.

What you’ll do

- Build and deploy ML/AI services. Design, develop, and ship ML models and AI systems that Product Engineering teams rely on. You write the model code, the API layer, the monitoring, and the tests. Not notebooks; production services.

- Design with LLMs and APIs. Use LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) as building blocks in production systems. You know when to call an LLM, when to fine-tune, when to use a classical model, and when to write a rule. You think about cost, latency, and quality together.

- Ship production software. Write clean, well-structured code with solid OOP, proper abstractions, error handling, and tests. Your code gets reviewed by SWEs and passes. CI/CD is how you work, not something you bolt on at the end.

- Partner with product and engineering. Translate business problems into ML solutions. Define API contracts with product engineers. Explain your approach clearly to non-ML partners and leave the room with alignment, not confusion.

- Evaluate and iterate fast. Build evaluation frameworks, run experiments, and make data-driven decisions about model and system performance. Ship and iterate; don’t wait for perfect.

- Ship AI-powered workflows. Put AI to work on your own processes: automate pipelines, build agentic workflows, and contribute reusable skills and context to Checkr’s agentic platform. The expectation is that our teams operate AI-first.

What you bring

- A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related technical field, or equivalent depth from experience

- 6+ years building software professionally, with at least 2 of those building ML systems that run in production

- Strong Python fluency; you write clean, testable, well-structured code with solid OOP instincts. Hands-on experience using LLM APIs in production systems: prompt engineering, structured outputs, function calling, cost management, and evaluation

- You’ve built and maintained APIs, worked with CI/CD pipelines, and shipped code that other engineers depend on

- Comfort with and enthusiasm for AI-assisted workflows; experience using LLMs, code-generation tools, or agentic systems in production or operational contexts is a strong signal

- You use AI tools (Copilot, Claude, etc.) to move faster, but you understand every line they produce. You can spot AI slop and you don’t ship it

- An A-player mindset with a strong bias for action: you raise the bar, move with urgency, stay resilient through ambiguity, and take ownership to deliver meaningful outcomes.

Nice to have

- Experience with MLOps platforms (MLflow, SageMaker, Vertex, or similar)

- Background in document processing, OCR, or information extraction

- Experience with PySpark or large-scale data processing

- Ruby experience (Checkr’s platform runs on Rails)

- Familiarity with compliance-sensitive domains (fintech, legal tech, HR tech)

- Working knowledge of dbt, Snowflake, or modern ELT/data transformation tools

- Competitive cash and equity compensation, and opportunity for advancement

title: Senior Data Analyst II
description:
- Shape the analytics strategy behind Zip’s next generation of financial products, driving data-informed decisions from launch through growth.

- Bring deep SQL, dbt, and product analytics expertise to solve complex business challenges, influence senior leaders, and build scalable analytics foundations for new product lines.

- Remote-first opportunity for US-based employees with the option to work in-person out of our Manhattan office

Why we're hiring this role

Zip is at an exciting inflection point. As we expand beyond our core BNPL product into new financial products, the Data Analytics team is looking for a Senior Data Analyst II to be the senior analytics voice for this growth frontier.

You'll partner with senior leaders across Product, Finance, Risk, and Operations to build the analytical foundations that will define how Zip evaluates, launches, and scales new product categories. You'll lead complex, high-impact analytical initiatives, from helping size market opportunity and measuring early product-market fit, to understanding customer eligibility, adoption, and retention across our expanding product suite.

This is a rare opportunity to shape analytics from the ground up for products that don't yet have established playbooks, where your work will directly influence strategic investment decisions and product direction.

Start your adventure with Zip

As a Senior Data Analyst II working with the business, you'll own the analytics that power Zip's most strategically important growth bets. You'll be the primary analytical partner for teams building new Zip products, helping them understand customer behavior, product performance and financial outcomes at each stage of the product lifecycle, from pre-launch through scaled adoption.

You'll operate in a highly ambiguous environment where the right questions are still being defined. You'll bring structure and rigor to that ambiguity, translating incomplete or conflicting signals into clear recommendations that guide product strategy, risk appetite, and go to market decisions.

Alongside delivering analysis, you'll build the scalable data models and shared metrics that will serve as the authoritative foundation for new product analytics as the initiative grows.

Interesting problems you’ll get to solve

- Lead end to end analytics for Zip's new product lines from opportunity sizing and launch readiness through post-launch performance and iteration.

- Partner with Product, Risk and Finance leaders to define success metrics, build reporting frameworks and create analytical infrastructure for products that are new to Zip's portfolio.

- Develop a deep understanding of the customer funnel and lifecycle for new financial products, including eligibility, application, approval, repayment and retention. Identify the levers that drive healthy unit economics.

- Analyze customer overlap, cross product adoption, and portfolio diversification to assess how new product verticals complement or expand Zip's existing BNPL customer base.

- Build market sizing, segmentation, and opportunity analyses that inform where and how Zip should invest in new product growth.

- Design, implement, and govern scalable analytics frameworks, including reusable data models, shared metrics, and analytical methodologies, purpose-built for new product categories where definitions must be established from scratch.

- Develop advanced analyses integrating behavioral, financial, and risk data to provide holistic, forward-looking views of product health and customer outcomes.

- Set and champion best practices for dbt data modeling, SQL performance, and analytical code quality as the new product analytics foundation is established.

- Advise VP and executive-level stakeholders by synthesizing complex analysis into concise narratives connecting insights to product strategy, financial impact, risk trade-offs and growth opportunity.

- Drive cross-functional alignment on metrics, definitions, and analytical approaches across Product, Finance, Risk, and Operations teams working on new products while escalating material decisions to leadership

- Raise the analytical bar across the team through mentorship, knowledge sharing, and thoughtful review of analytical approaches and outputs.

What you’ll bring to the team

- 8+ years of experience in data analytics, product analytics, business intelligence or a related analytical discipline, including experience in highly complex or ambiguous analytical environments.

- Deep SQL expertise and demonstrated experience designing efficient analytical solutions across large and complex datasets.

- Advanced experience with dbt and data modeling, including building scalable, reusable data models and trusted analytical foundations.

- Advanced experience with Tableau or comparable BI platforms, and experience developing scalable reporting and visualization solutions.

- Experience in fintech, consumer lending, or financial services analytics - ok with an understanding of customer credit, repayment behavior, and product risk dynamics is highly valued.

- Demonstrated experience leading complex, ambiguous analytical initiatives from problem definition through analysis, recommendation, and business impact, ideally including new product launches or 0-to-1 analytics buildouts.

- Experience partnering with senior leaders and influencing strategic decisions through clear, evidence-based analytical recommendations.

- Strong business acumen with the ability to connect product analytics to broader business drivers, including revenue, unit economics, customer retention, and risk across a diversified product portfolio.

- Experience establishing analytical standards, shared metrics or reusable frameworks that improve consistency and scalability across teams.

- Experience applying AI-enabled tools and emerging technologies to analytics workflows, automation or self-service capabilities.

- Demonstrated ability to mentor other analysts, elevate analytical rigor and contribute to stronger technical and problem-solving practices across a team.

What you’ll get in return

Zip is a place where you’ll get out what you put in. The newness of our sector means we need to move at pace and embrace change, and our promise to you when you join the team is that you’ll feel empowered and trusted to make big things happen quickly.

We want you to feel welcome and as though you have the support to be yourself, and care for yourself at work. Because it’s important to us that you make the most of the opportunities you’ll get to grow your skills and your career, and be surrounded by smart, friendly people and leaders that have your back.

We think these are just some of the best things about being a Zipster. We will also offer you:

- Flexible working culture

- Incentive programs

- Unlimited PTO

- Generous paid parental leave

- Leading family support policies

- Company-sponsored 401k match

- Learning and wellness subscription stipend
